questions.q: In the SR-5 signal construction, which sectors are bought long?
options: The top tercile by predicted score
The bottom tercile by predicted score
Whichever sector has the highest trading volume
All 11 sectors equally
questions.explain: The bottom tercile — sectors predicted to bounce back hardest — is bought long; the top tercile is sold short.

questions.q: Why are positions inverse-volatility weighted within each leg instead of equally weighted?
options: To guarantee the highest possible return
So calmer (lower-volatility) sectors receive more weight than choppier ones for the same conviction
Because Ridge regression requires inverse-volatility inputs
To eliminate the need for a position cap
questions.explain: Inverse-volatility weighting gives more weight to calmer sectors within a leg, rather than treating all names in the leg identically regardless of their volatility.

questions.q: What does 'dollar-neutral, 100% gross exposure' mean for the SR-5 book?
options: 100% long and 100% short, for 200% gross exposure
50% long and 50% short, so long and short dollar exposure are equal and net market exposure is near zero
All capital held in cash most of the time
Exposure limited to 50% of the long leg only
questions.explain: Dollar-neutral at 100% gross exposure means 50% long and 50% short — equal dollar exposure on each side, netting to near-zero market exposure.

questions.q: Why is there a 1-day lag between the Friday signal and Monday execution?
options: Stooq.com does not update data on Fridays
To avoid trading on a price or decision that wasn't actually knowable/actionable until the next session, avoiding lookahead
Because the C++ core needs an extra day to compute
Weekends require a mandatory cooldown period for ETFs
questions.explain: Computing the signal at Friday close and executing at Monday's session (rather than instantly) avoids lookahead — trading on information before it would actually be actionable.

questions.q: What does the VIX-regime overlay do in the low-VIX tercile?
options: Doubles gross exposure, since calm markets are safer
Cuts gross exposure to half-size, because the reversal effect is weak and not statistically significant when VIX is calm
Switches the model from Ridge to Random Forest
Removes the position cap entirely
questions.explain: Because the low-VIX tercile IC (≈-0.02, not significant) is much weaker than the high-VIX tercile IC (≈-0.11, significant), gross exposure is scaled to half-size when VIX is low.
